original_value: Here we propose the use of twist and glide symmetries to increase the equivalent refractive index in a helical guiding structure. Twist- and glide-symmetrical distributions are created with corrugations placed at both sides of a helical strip. Combined twist-and glide-symmetrical helical unit cells are studied in terms of their constituent parameters. The increase of the propagation constant is mainly controlled by the length of the corrugations. In our proposed helix antenna, twist and glide symmetry cells are used to reduce significantly the operational frequency compared with conventional helix antenna. Equivalently, for a given frequency of operation, the dimensions of helix are reduced with the use of higher symmetries. The theoretical results obtained for our proposed helical structure based on higher symmetries show a reduction of 42.2% in the antenna size maintaining a similar antenna performance when compared to conventional helix antennas.

result.paraphrase: We propose using twist and glide symmetries to raise the equivalent refractive index in a helical guiding structure. Twist- and glide-symmetric patterns are formed by placing corrugations on both sides of a helical strip. Combined twist- and glide-symmetric helical unit cells are analyzed according to their constituent parameters. The propagation constant increase is governed mainly by the corrugation length. In the proposed helix antenna, twist and glide symmetry cells are used to substantially lower the operating frequency relative to a conventional helix antenna. Likewise, at a fixed operating frequency, the helix dimensions are reduced by using higher symmetries. Theoretical results for the proposed higher-symmetry helical structure indicate a 42.2% reduction in antenna size while maintaining similar performance compared with conventional helix antennas.
